blocks.text: The City's own counts differ, probably by definition and date. Its Tourism Development Framework gives about 45,000 direct jobs and about 150,000 in total (City of Cape Town, Tourism Development Framework 2019 to 2024, p3). That direct count is under half the City's 2024 figure. The framework's figures imply about 3.3 total jobs for each direct job (computed). Applied to the provincial ambition, 300,000 total jobs would mean about 90,000 direct jobs, fewer than Cape Town alone counted in 2024 on its own definition (computed). The ambition can be judged only once its definition and base are fixed.

edits.reason: Assessment 4, "Cape Town tourism jobs": 106,707 direct (City, 2025) against the TDF's direct count (TDF p3, about 45,000), probably definitional, I18 reconciles. Assessment 5, FA20 (Medium): the TDF ratio of about 3.3 total jobs per direct job gives I18 a test for the 300,000. 150,000 / 45,000 = 3.33; 300,000 / 3.33 = 90,000; 90,000 / 45,000 = 2. Review: 'by definition and date'; the implication stated: on the total-jobs reading, Cape Town alone counts more direct jobs (106,707) than the provincial ambition implies (about 90,000).

blocks.text: **Wesgro's own arrivals target outruns every modelled path to 2030.** Wesgro seeks 800,000 to 1 million new international arrivals over FY26 to FY30 (Wesgro, Strategic Plan 2025/26 to 2029/30, p20).
